title: GPU Pool Control Bar — Compact Health Strip + Dynamic Burst Editor
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a compact, single-line control bar for the Redwood Console GPU pool detail page that surfaces critical health signals, cost per-token estimate, and a lightweight burst/autoscale editor. The goal is to reduce cognitive load for on-call engineers and platform owners while keeping fast access to actions (pause pool, force-scale, set burst window). This design should work inside the existing pool detail header and be responsive for narrow panes.
objectives: Surface at-a-glance health: SLO status, utilization, recent errors
Expose quickest path to change burst and autoscale settings without leaving page
Provide an inline cost estimate and expected latency delta for burst actions
Maintain accessibility, keyboard focus and clear affordances for destructive actions
Fit into both full and compact pool list/detail contexts
acceptance_criteria: Compact control bar implemented as single horizontal strip in mockups and interactive prototype
Each health chip has tooltip explaining metric and link to full metric page
Burst editor supports quick presets (30s, 2m, 10m) and a custom slider with live cost estimate
Primary destructive action (pause pool) requires confirmation modal and shows estimated impact on queued requests
Design reviewed with Eng runtime and Product; feedback addressed and annotated in Figma
decisions: Use three-state health chips (Good / Degraded / Critical) with color and icon to match console palette
Inline cost estimate uses token-rate approximation tied to model tier; show approximate currency per minute
Burst editing will be optimistic-only in UI and call an API endpoint that validates feasibility; UI shows validation errors inline
Compact mode collapses detailed metrics into a single ellipsis menu but keeps primary actions visible
comments: 2026-02-25 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff — sketched 3 layouts (stacked, strip, floating). Chose horizontal strip for minimal vertical footprint.
2026-02-27 - Marco Liu: Engineering review — confirmed feasibility for inline validation and cost query; asked for open/close animation specs and keyboard focus path.
2026-03-01 - Sofia Ramirez (PM): Product note — prioritize quick burst presets and show customer-facing cost delta for transparency. Flagged compliance with existing billing labels.
2026-03-04 - Design critique: Suggested increasing contrast on degraded state and adding microcopy for 'burst uses reserved burst pool credits'.
2026-03-07 - Prototype usability test (5 internal participants): users completed burst edit in 2 clicks on average; requested clearer undo affordance. Added ephemeral 'undo' toast for 30s.
2026-03-10 - Marco Liu: In Review — handed over Figma frames and interactive prototype. Engineering pointed out edge case when pool is already at capacity; added validation message flows.
